name: Hal
look: A weathered, broad-shouldered man near fifty with a close-cropped grey beard, a white scar through one eyebrow and two fingers missing on his left hand, a quilted gambeson over a brown tunic, leather bracers and heavy boots.
combat: a veteran: patient, hard to hit, hits hard
personality: Calm, dry and demanding; has seen too many young fools die and would rather shout at you now than bury you later.
values: discipline, a steady guard, people who get back up
fears: sending green recruits to a real fight
authority: Teaches the garrison's recruits and anyone else he thinks worth it.
concerns: Bram is too eager by half; a stranger who can't hold a shield won't last a week on the roads.

windup.text: Every blow winds up first: step back out of reach, or meet it with a shield.
windup.line: Watch the shoulder, not the blade. It winds up; you step out or you block.
windup.lead: Every blow winds up first: step out of reach or block it.

brea.text: Mother Brea at the inn patches up every recruit who gets clumsy with a blade.
brea.line: Get cut, you go to Mother Brea at the inn. Everybody does, sooner or later.
brea.lead: Mother Brea at the inn patches up the recruits' cuts.

persuaded_by: seeing someone take a hit and get back up
style: Short, dry orders; a rare grin; never wastes words.

samples: Shield up. Up! You'd be dead twice.
Good. Now do it when it matters.
Everyone thinks they'll be brave. Most just get hit.
voice.habits: Gives orders in two or three words; praises with 'Good.'; counts mistakes out loud.
voice.never: flatters, rushes a lesson, or fights for real in the yard
voice.greeting: Looks you up and down: 'Here to watch, or here to learn?'

goals: Turn Bram into a soldier who'll live
dislikes: show-offs, people who drop their shield

superstition.text: Hal would want to know how it works.
